answer: Picture a lone operator hiding many agent masks behind one inference pipeline, pale and smooth as ivory. To resist this, the economy hands every identity a distinct, skill-heavy task that must finish inside the same narrow deadline window. One mind cannot puppet a frozen tundra of masks at once; serving them serially blows the clock, so the fake swarm stalls while honest parallel capacity passes. That stall sends a ripple through the reputation ledger, freezing payouts. The attacker now pays for real concurrent compute, not cheap key minting.
